title: Build Your First AI Automation: Leads, Emails and a Bot
artifact: One automation running for your own business — lead capture, an AI-written first reply, a three-email follow-up and a FAQ bot — plus the brief, prompts and blueprint to build the next one
description: Walk in with the questions your customers keep asking. Walk out at 4:00 PM with an automation running for your business: every new enquiry gets a personal AI-written reply within the hour, three follow-up emails that stop once the lead replies, and a Telegram bot that answers from your own price list. Four hours, offline, no coding.
mission: An offline space for non-techies to put AI to work, one real use-case project at a time.

lead.name: Neeraj Kanoi
lead.bio: Neeraj is the solo growth lead at Wokelo AI. With no team under him, he is building Wokelo’s growth funnel single-handedly, with AI doing the work a team would. On 25 October he shows how that works, then builds a smaller version with you, for your business.

lines: Leave with a machine that follows up.
hero.sub: Four hours. Five parts. One automation, running.

artifactsHeading: You leave with five working parts.

outcomes: The business brief: one page that teaches every automation your offer, your prices, your tone, and the things it must never say
Lead capture: a live form that drops every enquiry into one Google Sheet, with nothing copied by hand
The AI first reply: a personal email in your voice, written from your brief and sent within the hour, during your working hours
The follow-up sequence: three emails on day 2, day 5 and day 9 that stop once the lead replies, plus the same pipeline to send a campaign to people who asked to hear from you
The FAQ bot: a Telegram bot that answers customer questions from your own price list, and hands the conversation to you when it is not sure

agenda.title: Neeraj’s funnel, then yours on paper
agenda.body: Neeraj walks through the growth system he runs alone at Wokelo AI: what runs without him, and what he still does by hand. Then you map your own: where enquiries come from, the first thing people ask, and the one step you want them to take. You write the one-page business brief that every automation will read.

agenda.title: Lead in, AI reply out
agenda.body: Build the first workflow in Make: a form drops each enquiry into a Google Sheet, Gemini writes a personal reply from your brief, and Gmail sends it. It stays in draft mode until you have read five replies and trust them.

agenda.title: Break
agenda.body: Chai. Table captains check that every first workflow has run once, end to end.

agenda.title: The follow-up sequence
agenda.body: Write three follow-ups for day 2, day 5 and day 9 from your brief, then let the sheet schedule them. Every send checks your inbox first and stops the moment the lead replies. The same pipeline sends one campaign to people who asked to hear from you.

agenda.title: The FAQ bot
agenda.body: Create a Telegram bot in two minutes, then give it your price list, your FAQ and one rule: if the answer is not in your facts, it says so and passes the question to you. Test it from your own phone.

agenda.title: Break it, then switch it on
agenda.body: Send a fake lead from your phone through the whole machine. Run the checklist: wrong names, invented prices, double sends, the spam folder, a bot that guesses. Fix what matters, switch it on, and export the blueprint you will open again on Tuesday.

faqs.a: Neeraj Kanoi, the solo growth lead at Wokelo AI. He is building Wokelo’s growth funnel single-handedly, with AI doing the work a team would. He opens the session by walking through how that system runs, then builds a smaller version with the room. Yogesh and Subham Kanoi host alongside him, and every table of eight has a captain.

faqs.q: Do I need to know coding?
faqs.a: No. Every step happens in visual tools: you connect boxes, paste in your facts, and write instructions in plain English, Hindi or Bangla. If you can fill in a Google Form and send an email, you can build this. A captain sits at every table to unblock you when a connection fails.

One automation for your own business: a form that captures each enquiry into a Google Sheet, an AI-written first reply in your voice, sent within the hour during your working hours, three follow-up emails on day 2, day 5 and day 9 that stop once the lead replies, and a Telegram bot that answers from your price list. You also keep the brief, the prompts and the exported blueprint, so the second one does not start from scratch.

Not on the day. The build runs on free tiers: Make’s free plan, a free Gemini API key from Google AI Studio, Gmail, Google Sheets and Telegram. Free tiers limit how often an automation runs and how much it sends, and those limits change. We show you how to stay inside them, and what the first paid upgrade would be if your volume grows. The ticket does not include any paid plan.

faqs.q: Can I use my own business?
faqs.a: Please do. Bring your price list or menu, the five questions customers ask most, and the email you send when someone enquires. Shop owners, clinics, coaches, freelancers and agency owners get the most out of the day, because the automation is theirs on Monday. No business yet? We hand you a sample one at the table.

Because anyone can create a working Telegram bot in two minutes, free. WhatsApp’s official bot access needs a Meta business account, business verification and a dedicated number, and Meta charges for many message types; setting it up takes days, not an afternoon. The bot’s brain — your facts, your tone, your hand-over rule — is the same on both. We build it on Telegram and show you the path to WhatsApp once your business is verified.

Not the way we build it. Every email goes to someone who contacted you or asked to hear from you, every sequence stops when they reply, and campaigns carry a way to opt out. We do not buy lists, scrape contacts or send cold blasts, and Gmail would block you if you tried. If you want to email ten thousand strangers, skip this Sunday.

No. It is offline in Salt Lake, Kolkata, and there is no recording or livestream. The room is the method: fifty people, tables of eight, and a captain at each table who can look at your screen when a connection fails.

faqs.q: Can I attend with only a phone?
faqs.a: Not usefully. Building the automations needs a laptop browser and a real screen. Your phone is for testing: you send the fake lead and talk to your bot from it. Bring a laptop and a charger — power strips and table Wi-Fi are provided at the venue.

faqs.q: What about customer data and privacy?
faqs.a: Build with test leads, not your real customer list. Do not bring confidential client files, and do not paste anything you would not want stored by a third-party service: free AI tiers may use what you send to improve their products. When you switch on with real customers, tell them how you will contact them, and follow your employer’s AI policy.

faqs.q: Where is it, and what is included?
faqs.a: Offline in Salt Lake, Kolkata, on Sunday 25 October 2026, 12:00 PM to 4:00 PM. The ticket is ₹699 for the four-hour build, the table captains, and the brief, prompts and blueprint you keep. There are 50 seats. The exact venue is shared after reservation. Full refund up to 48 hours before the session; venue holds are released 15 minutes after kickoff.

localFaqs.a: The workshop is held in Salt Lake Sector 1, Kolkata. The venue is easily accessible via the Kolkata Metro Green Line (Salt Lake / City Centre stations) and is a short 5-minute cab ride from Ultadanga/EM Bypass. Exact venue address and Google Maps directions are emailed immediately upon booking.

localFaqs.q: Is parking available at the venue?
localFaqs.a: Yes, designated two-wheeler and four-wheeler street and venue parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis in Sector 1.

localFaqs.q: What hardware and software do I need to bring?
localFaqs.a: Bring a laptop (Mac or Windows) with a working browser and charger, and your phone with Telegram installed. High-speed table Wi-Fi and power strips are provided. Nothing needs installing on the laptop: every tool runs in the browser.
